blocks.text: There were no significant changes in the human rights situation in Niue during the year. There were no credible reports of significant human rights abuses. The government took credible steps to identify and punish officials who committed human rights abuses.
There were no reports the government or its agents committed arbitrary or unlawful killings.
There were no reports of coerced abortion or involuntary sterilization on the part of government authorities.

The law did not explicitly provide for freedom of expression; however, the democratic system and the judiciary protected freedom of expression, including for the media, and there were no reports of the government restricting this freedom.

Freedom of Association and Collective Bargaining No laws existed guaranteeing freedom of association, collective bargaining, or the right to strike. The law did not specifically prohibit antiunion discrimination, nor did it require the reinstatement of workers fired for union activity. The law prohibited public employees from undertaking industrial action. The Niue Public Service Association represented employees of the Public Service Commission on matters affecting conditions of employment. There were no independent trade unions or nongovernmental organizations supporting the rights of workers in the private sector. There were no available reports regarding government recognition of freedom of association or the right to collective bargaining. Forced or Compulsory Labor There were no laws prohibiting forced or compulsory labor for private sector labor. Acceptable Work Conditions Wage and Hour Laws Regulations detailed the Public Service Commission’s wage and working hour obligations for government employees. No reports were available for private sector employees. Occupational Safety and Health Regulations detailed the Public Service Commission’s occupational and health obligations to government employees. No reports were available for private sector employees. Wage, Hour, and OSH Enforcement There were no reports regarding enforcement of minimum wage, overtime, and occupational health and safety laws. There was no law specifically pertaining to those who worked in the informal sector, such as those making handicrafts and other goods, and there were no wage, hour, or other labor protections provided by the law in these situations.

Disappearance There were no reports of enforced disappearances by or on behalf of government authorities. Prolonged Detention without Charges The law prohibited arbitrary arrest and detention and required good cause be established for the issuance of a warrant or for an arrest without a warrant.
See the Department of State’s annual International Religious Freedom Report at http://www.state.gov/religiousfreedomreport/.

The law did not clearly criminalize all forms of human trafficking or remove the requirement of force, fraud, or coercion for child sex trafficking. There were no reports that traffickers exploited domestic or foreign victims in the country or exploited nationals as victims abroad.

blocks.subsection: a. Torture and Cruel, Inhuman, or Degrading Treatment or Punishment
blocks.text: Punishment The law prohibited such practices, and there were no reports that government officials employed them.

Child Labor There were no laws pertaining to the minimum age of employment, including for hazardous work. See the Department of Labor’s Findings on the Worst Forms of Child Labor at https://www.dol.gov/agencies/ilab/resources/reports/child-labor/findings/. Child Marriage Parental consent was required to solemnize the marriage of any woman or girl under age 19, or man under 21. With parental permission, the legal marriageable age was 15 for girls and 18 for men; however, marriage occurring in contradiction to this were not invalidated. There was no available data on the prevalence of child, early, or forced marriage. Information was not available on government measures to prevent or mitigate early marriage.

The law did not reference refugees or asylum seekers, although provisions outlined immigration procedures and procedures for the removal of persons in the country illegally. There were no reports of persons seeking asylum. Provision of First Asylum The law did not provide for granting asylum or refugee status, and the government had no system for providing protection to refugees. The principal immigration officer had wide discretionary powers under immigration laws and could allow noncitizens to remain, including on humanitarian grounds.

blocks.subsection: d. Acts of Antisemitism and Antisemitic Incitement
blocks.text: There was no known Jewish community; there were no reports of antisemitic acts.
